1:1.t: Philemon was a believer in Colossae; Onesimus was his slave, who had apparently run away and met Paul in prison (Colossians 4:9). Paul sends him back with this letter.

1:2.t: "Our sister": the KJV's "beloved"; many early manuscripts read "our sister". Apphia may have been Philemon's wife and Archippus his son (compare Colossians 4:17).

1:5.t: "All His holy people": the KJV's "all saints".

1:9.t: "An old man": the KJV's "the aged"; the Greek presbytes may also be read presbeutes, "ambassador" (compare Ephesians 6:20).

1:12.t: "Receive him": the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts do not have these words.
"Hearts ... very heart" (Greek splanchna): the KJV's "bowels". See 2 Corinthians 6:12.

1:20.t: "In the Lord": the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts read "in Christ".
"Hearts ... very heart" (Greek splanchna): the KJV's "bowels". See 2 Corinthians 6:12.

1:7.t: "Hearts ... very heart" (Greek splanchna): the KJV's "bowels". See 2 Corinthians 6:12.

1:11.t: "Useless ... useful" (Greek achrestos ... euchrestos): a wordplay on the name Onesimus, which means "useful".

1:16.t: "No longer as a slave ... as a dear brother": Paul does not directly command freedom, but he transforms the relationship. Many see here the seed of the Christian rejection of slavery.
